title: St John Ambulance: do not sponge a fever, because of overcooling
summary: A light cover, cool drinks, and the recommended dose of paracetamol. No aspirin under 16. The page gives temperature thresholds for calling about a baby.
body: St John Ambulance's fever page says to make the person comfortable and keep them cool, ideally in bed with a sheet or a light duvet. Do not sponge them, because of the risk of overcooling. Give plenty of cool drinks to replace fluid lost in sweat. If they feel unwell, give the recommended dose of paracetamol for an adult, or paracetamol syrup for a child. Do not give aspirin to anyone under 16. Monitor response until they recover. If you are worried, seek medical advice. For a child, contact 111 or the GP surgery if they are under 3 months and the temperature is over 38°C, or 3 to 6 months and over 39°C, or the temperature has lasted more than five days, or they do not want to eat or drink, or they are dehydrated. The dehydration examples begin with nappies that are not very wet and sunken features. The extract cuts off at "sunken," so the rest of that sign list is not completed here.
